# Scope

This document reproduces every figure, table and statistical test reported in the manuscript *"The informal settlement gap in African urban growth research: a systematic review of 183 studies"*. Exploratory analyses performed during the review but not reported in the paper (expansion-rate regressions, logistic models of prediction uptake, driver co-occurrence) live in `01_exploratory_analysis.Rmd`.

The analytical corpus is 183 peer-reviewed studies screened in from an initial 14,282 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus on 27 October 2025 (see Methods §Literature search and selection).

# Package setup

```{r packages}
# Core data manipulation and visualisation
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# Statistical analysis
library(rstatix)        # pairwise tests and effect sizes
library(effectsize)     # Cramér's V

# Geospatial / mapping
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
library(viridis)

# Consistent theme
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40", size = 11),
      legend.position = "right",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)

# Palette
pal_blue   <- c("#185FA5", "#378ADD", "#85B7EB", "#B5D4F4", "#E6F1FB")
pal_teal   <- c("#085041", "#0F6E56", "#1D9E75", "#5DCAA5", "#9FE1CB")
pal_coral  <- c("#993C1D", "#D85A30", "#F0997B", "#F5C4B3")
pal_amber  <- c("#854F0B", "#BA7517", "#EF9F27", "#FAC775")

pal_region <- c(
  "Western Africa"  = "#185FA5",
  "Eastern Africa"  = "#1D9E75",
  "Northern Africa" = "#D85A30",
  "Southern Africa" = "#BA7517",
  "Middle Africa"   = "#534AB7"
)

pal_size <- c(
  "Megacity"          = "#185FA5",
  "Large City"        = "#378ADD",
  "Medium-sized City" = "#1D9E75",
  "Small City"        = "#5DCAA5",
  "Very Small City"   = "#9FE1CB"
)
```

# Data loading and preparation

```{r load-data}
df <- read_csv("../data/urban_growth_cleaned.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

cat("Dataset dimensions:", nrow(df), "rows ×", ncol(df), "columns\n")
cat("Study coverage:",
    min(df$pub_year, na.rm = TRUE), "–", max(df$pub_year, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")
cat("Countries:", n_distinct(df$country),
    "| Cities:", n_distinct(df$city), "\n")

stopifnot(nrow(df) == 183)  # analytical corpus from Methods §Literature search
```

## Apply 2025 UN city-size classification

City size follows the United Nations population thresholds used in the manuscript:
megacity > 10 M; large 5–10 M; medium 1–5 M; small 250 k–1 M; very small < 250 k.

```{r city-size}
classify_city <- function(pop) {
  case_when(
    is.na(pop)   ~ "Unknown",
    pop > 10e6   ~ "Megacity",
    pop >= 5e6   ~ "Large City",
    pop >= 1e6   ~ "Medium-sized City",
    pop >= 250e3 ~ "Small City",
    TRUE         ~ "Very Small City"
  )
}

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    city_size = factor(
      classify_city(population),
      levels = c("Megacity", "Large City", "Medium-sized City",
                 "Small City", "Very Small City", "Unknown")
    ),
    lat_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(latitude)),
    lon_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(longitude)),
    region  = ifelse(specific_region %in%
                       c("Unknown", "Western Africa, Middle Africa"),
                     "Unknown", specific_region),
    # Three-period classification used throughout the manuscript
    period = case_when(
      pub_year %in% 2015:2018 ~ "2015-2018",
      pub_year %in% 2019:2022 ~ "2019-2022",
      pub_year %in% 2023:2025 ~ "2023-2025",
      TRUE                    ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
```

# Temporal trends — Figure 2 and Table S2

## Figure 2 — annual research output

```{r fig2-temporal, fig.cap="Figure 2. Temporal distribution of selected papers on urban growth in Africa, 2015–2025."}
pub_trend <- df %>%
  count(pub_year) %>%
  mutate(
    informal = map_int(
      pub_year,
      ~ sum(df$pub_year == .x & df$informal_dev_bin == 1)
    )
  )

ggplot(pub_trend, aes(x = pub_year)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = n), fill = pal_blue[1], width = 0.7) +
  geom_col(aes(y = informal), fill = pal_coral[2], width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(y = n, label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5, colour = "grey30") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2015:2025) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = "Annual research output on African urban growth, 2015–2025",
    subtitle = "Informal-settlement-focused studies shown in coral",
    x = NULL, y = "Number of studies"
  )
```

The manuscript reports: 7.5 studies/yr 2015–2018, 22 in 2019, 14 in 2020, 18 each in 2021 and 2022, 39 in 2023, 24 in 2024, 18 in 2025. Informal-settlement path: 0 in 2015–2016, first in 2017 (Shabat & Tapamo), 1–2/yr through 2022, 6 in 2023, 4 in 2024, 2 in 2025.

## Table S2 — urban hierarchy composition by period

```{r tableS2-hierarchy-period}
ts2 <- df %>%
  filter(city_size != "Unknown", !is.na(period)) %>%
  count(period, city_size) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) %>%
  select(period, city_size, pct) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = city_size, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(n_period = df %>%
           filter(city_size != "Unknown", !is.na(period)) %>%
           count(period) %>% pull(n)) %>%
  select(period, n_period, everything())

kable(
  ts2,
  caption = "Table S2 | Urban-hierarchy composition of African urban growth studies, by period. Row percentages sum to 100.",
  col.names = c("Period", "n", "Megacity", "Large", "Medium",
                "Small", "Very small")
) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```

### Chi-square: period × urban hierarchy

Reported in the manuscript as χ²(8) = 18.24, *p* = 0.020, *n* = 164, Cramér's V = 0.24.

```{r chi-period-hierarchy}
tab_ph <- df %>%
  filter(city_size != "Unknown", !is.na(period)) %>%
  with(table(period, city_size))

chi_ph <- chisq.test(tab_ph)
cramer_ph <- cramers_v(tab_ph)

print(chi_ph)
print(cramer_ph)
cat(sprintf(
  "\nReported: χ²(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f, n = %d, Cramér's V = %.2f\n",
  chi_ph$parameter, chi_ph$statistic, chi_ph$p.value,
  sum(tab_ph), cramer_ph$Cramers_v
))
```

# Geographic distribution — Figure 3

## Top-10 countries by study count

```{r top10-table}
top10 <- df %>%
  filter(!country %in% c("Africa/Multiple", "West Africa")) %>%
  count(country, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_head(n = 10)

kable(top10,
      caption = "Top-10 countries by research output",
      col.names = c("Country", "Studies")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```

Expected (manuscript): Nigeria 34, Ethiopia 29, Egypt 24, Ghana 20, Algeria 14, South Africa 11, Tanzania 11, Morocco 9. Together the eight leading contributors account for 83.1 % of the corpus.

## Figure 3a — choropleth of studies per country

```{r africa-base, results='hide'}
africa <- ne_countries(continent = "Africa", returnclass = "sf", scale = "medium")

country_lookup <- tibble(
  country_data = unique(df$country),
  country_ne = case_when(
    country_data == "Democratic Republic of Congo" ~ "Dem. Rep. Congo",
    country_data == "West Africa"      ~ NA_character_,
    country_data == "Africa/Multiple"  ~ NA_character_,
    TRUE                               ~ country_data
  )
)

country_counts <- df %>%
  left_join(country_lookup, by = c("country" = "country_data")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(country_ne)) %>%
  count(country_ne, name = "studies")

africa_map <- africa %>%
  left_join(country_counts, by = c("name" = "country_ne")) %>%
  mutate(studies = replace_na(studies, 0))
```

```{r fig3a-studies-map, fig.cap="Figure 3a. Geographic distribution of urban growth research.", fig.height=8}
ggplot(africa_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = studies), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt",
                       breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 20, 35), name = "Studies (n)") +
  geom_sf_text(data = africa_map %>% filter(studies >= 5),
               aes(label = paste0(name, "\n(", studies, ")")),
               size = 2.8, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-20, 55), ylim = c(-37, 38)) +
  labs(title = "Geographic distribution of urban growth research",
       subtitle = "Number of studies per country, 2015–2025") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40"))
```

## Figure 3b — choropleth of informal-settlement research

```{r fig3b-informal-map, fig.cap="Figure 3b. Geographic distribution of informal-settlement research.", fig.height=8}
country_inf <- df %>%
  left_join(country_lookup, by = c("country" = "country_data")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(country_ne)) %>%
  group_by(country_ne) %>%
  summarise(rate = mean(informal_dev_bin),
            n_total = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_total >= 3)

africa_inf <- africa %>%
  left_join(country_inf, by = c("name" = "country_ne"))

ggplot(africa_inf) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = rate), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1,
                       labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                       na.value = "grey90",
                       name = "Informal\nfocus rate") +
  geom_sf_text(data = africa_inf %>% filter(!is.na(rate), rate > 0),
               aes(label = sprintf("%s\n%.0f%%", name, 100 * rate)),
               size = 2.8, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-20, 55), ylim = c(-37, 38)) +
  labs(title = "Geographic distribution of informal-settlement research",
       subtitle = "Share of studies per country explicitly studying informality",
       caption = "Countries with ≥ 3 studies only") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "grey40"))
```

# Informal-settlement analysis — Figure 4 and chi-square

## Figure 4a — informal focus by sub-region

```{r fig4a-informal-region, fig.cap="Figure 4a. Share of urban growth studies explicitly focusing on informal settlements by African sub-region."}
informal_region <- df %>%
  filter(region != "Unknown") %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(total = n(),
            informal = sum(informal_dev_bin),
            rate = informal / total, .groups = "drop")

ggplot(informal_region, aes(x = reorder(region, rate), y = rate, fill = region)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%d / %d (%.1f%%)", informal, total, 100 * rate)),
            hjust = -0.05, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_region) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Informal-focused research by African sub-region",
       x = NULL, y = "Informal-focus rate") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Figure 4b — informal focus by urban hierarchy

```{r fig4b-informal-size, fig.cap="Figure 4b. Proportion of informal-settlement-focused studies across African urban hierarchy."}
informal_size <- df %>%
  filter(city_size != "Unknown") %>%
  group_by(city_size) %>%
  summarise(total = n(),
            informal = sum(informal_dev_bin),
            rate = informal / total, .groups = "drop")

ggplot(informal_size, aes(x = city_size, y = rate, fill = city_size)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * rate)),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_size) +
  labs(title = "Informal-focused studies by city-size class",
       x = NULL, y = "Informal focus rate") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```

### Chi-square: urban hierarchy × informal focus

Reported in the manuscript as χ²(4) = 12.86, *p* = 0.012, *n* = 164, Cramér's V = 0.28.

```{r chi-hierarchy-informal}
tab_hi <- df %>%
  filter(city_size != "Unknown") %>%
  with(table(city_size, informal_dev_bin))

chi_hi <- chisq.test(tab_hi)
cramer_hi <- cramers_v(tab_hi)

print(chi_hi)
print(cramer_hi)
cat(sprintf(
  "\nReported: χ²(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f, n = %d, Cramér's V = %.2f\n",
  chi_hi$parameter, chi_hi$statistic, chi_hi$p.value,
  sum(tab_hi), cramer_hi$Cramers_v
))
```

# Methodological landscape — Figure 5

The method categorisation follows the taxonomy defined in Methods §Analysis approach:
*traditional* (maximum likelihood classification, cellular automata, regression-based models),
*machine learning* (SVM, random forests), *deep learning* (CNN, CA-ANN, MLP-Markov).

## Figure 5a — mapping method share by period

```{r fig5a-mapping-methods, fig.cap="Figure 5a. Annual proportion of mapping tasks by method type."}
mapping_period <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(period), !is.na(mapping_method_type)) %>%
  count(period, mapping_method_type) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(mapping_period,
       aes(x = period, y = share, fill = mapping_method_type)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Traditional" = pal_blue[1],
                               "Machine learning" = pal_teal[3],
                               "Deep learning" = pal_coral[2])) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Methodological composition of mapping tasks, by period",
       x = NULL, y = "Share of mapping tasks",
       fill = "Method type")
```

Expected (manuscript): traditional 66.9 % overall; ML in mapping grew from 20.0 % in 2015–2018 to 44.2 % in 2023–2025; DL barely features in mapping.

## Figure 5b — projection method share by period

```{r fig5b-projection-methods, fig.cap="Figure 5b. Annual proportion of projection tasks by method type."}
projection_period <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(period), !is.na(projection_method_type)) %>%
  count(period, projection_method_type) %>%
  group_by(period) %>%
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

ggplot(projection_period,
       aes(x = period, y = share, fill = projection_method_type)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Traditional" = pal_blue[1],
                               "Machine learning" = pal_teal[3],
                               "Deep learning" = pal_coral[2])) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(title = "Methodological composition of projection tasks, by period",
       x = NULL, y = "Share of projection tasks",
       fill = "Method type")
```

Expected (manuscript): traditional 68.8 % overall (CA-Markov 42.5 % of projections); DL 41.2 % of 2023–2025 projections, 66.7 % of 2024.

# Spatial typologies — Figure 6 and Table 1

## Spatial typology primary classification

```{r spatial-primary-prep}
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    spatial_primary = case_when(
      str_detect(spatial_form, "^peripheralization|^Peripheralisation") ~ "Peripheralisation",
      str_detect(spatial_form, "^Fragmentation")                        ~ "Fragmentation",
      str_detect(spatial_form, "^densification|^Densification")         ~ "Densification",
      str_detect(spatial_form, "^Ribbon")                               ~ "Ribbon",
      str_detect(spatial_form, "^Leapfrog")                             ~ "Leapfrog",
      TRUE                                                              ~ "Unknown"
    )
  )
```

## Figure 6a — overall spatial-typology frequency

```{r fig6a-typology, fig.cap="Figure 6a. Overall frequency of spatial typologies identified across the reviewed studies."}
spatial_overall <- df %>%
  filter(spatial_primary != "Unknown") %>%
  count(spatial_primary) %>%
  mutate(share = n / sum(n))

ggplot(spatial_overall,
       aes(x = reorder(spatial_primary, -share), y = share,
           fill = spatial_primary)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * share)),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Peripheralisation" = "#185FA5",
                               "Fragmentation"     = "#1D9E75",
                               "Densification"     = "#534AB7",
                               "Ribbon"            = "#BA7517",
                               "Leapfrog"          = "#D85A30")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(title = "Overall frequency of spatial typologies",
       x = NULL, y = "Share of occurrences") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Expected (manuscript): peripheralisation 58.9 %, fragmentation 15.5 %, densification 10.1 %, ribbon 7.8 %, leapfrog 7.8 %.

## Table 1 — typology by driver

```{r table1-driver-typology}
# Expand primary_driver to the categories reported in Table 1
driver_lookup <- c(
  "demography"    = "Population growth and migration",
  "migration"     = "Population growth and migration",
  "planning"      = "Planning regulation",
  "roads"         = "Road and transport expansion",
  "transport"    = "Road and transport expansion",
  "economy"       = "Economic development",
  "industry"      = "Industrial activity"
)

t1 <- df %>%
  filter(spatial_primary != "Unknown",
         !is.na(primary_driver),
         primary_driver != "Unknown") %>%
  mutate(driver = coalesce(driver_lookup[tolower(primary_driver)], primary_driver)) %>%
  count(driver, spatial_primary) %>%
  group_by(driver) %>%
  mutate(share = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1),
         total = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(driver, total, spatial_primary, share) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = spatial_primary, values_from = share,
              values_fill = 0) %>%
  arrange(desc(total)) %>%
  distinct(driver, .keep_all = TRUE)

kable(
  t1,
  caption = "Table 1 | Spatial typology distribution by driver of urban growth. Percentages are shares of occurrences within each driver and sum to 100 across rows (deviations due to rounding). Rows ordered by n.",
  col.names = c("Driver", "n", "Peripheralisation", "Fragmentation",
                "Densification", "Ribbon", "Leapfrog")
) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```

# Scenario analysis — Table 2

The manuscript reports 108 studies that project urban growth forward, of which only 16 construct more than one future (52 scenarios in total).

```{r scenario-overview}
scenario_studies <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(scenario_count), scenario_count >= 1)

multi_scenario <- scenario_studies %>%
  filter(scenario_count >= 2)

cat("Projection studies (total):      ", nrow(scenario_studies), "\n")
cat("Multi-scenario studies:          ", nrow(multi_scenario), "\n")
cat("Total scenarios across studies:  ", sum(multi_scenario$scenario_count), "\n")
```

## Table 2 — scenario themes

```{r table2-scenario-themes}
# scenario_theme is a semicolon-separated list of themes per study
theme_counts <- multi_scenario %>%
  separate_rows(scenario_theme, sep = ";\\s*") %>%
  filter(scenario_theme != "") %>%
  mutate(scenario_theme = str_trim(scenario_theme)) %>%
  count(scenario_theme, name = "scenarios") %>%
  mutate(
    studies = map_int(scenario_theme,
                      ~ multi_scenario %>%
                        filter(str_detect(scenario_theme, fixed(.x))) %>%
                        nrow()),
    share   = round(100 * scenarios / sum(scenarios), 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(scenarios))

kable(
  theme_counts,
  caption = "Table 2 | Scenario themes identified across the 16 multi-scenario studies of African urban growth. Each study tested one or more scenarios; counts total 52.",
  col.names = c("Scenario theme", "Scenarios", "Studies", "Share (%)")
) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```

## Scenario horizons

```{r scenario-horizons}
horizon_counts <- multi_scenario %>%
  separate_rows(scenario_year, sep = ";\\s*") %>%
  filter(scenario_year != "") %>%
  mutate(scenario_year = as.integer(scenario_year)) %>%
  count(scenario_year, name = "studies") %>%
  arrange(desc(studies))

kable(horizon_counts,
      caption = "Scenario horizon years across the 16 multi-scenario studies.",
      col.names = c("Horizon year", "Studies")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

Expected (manuscript): 2030 (9 studies), 2035 (3), 2025 and 2050 (2 each), longest 2076 (Jagarnath et al. 2019).
